prompt: In 2026, rank these platforms by the share of U.S. adults who say they use them.
explanation: YouTube reaches 84% of U.S. adults and Instagram 51%. Snapchat (26%) is now ahead of X, which slipped from 21% in 2025 to 18% in 2026.

source.title: Americans' Use of Social Media in 2026 (Social Media Fact Sheet)

caveat: Measures the share of adults who say they ever use each platform, not daily active users: no single source publishes comparable U.S. daily users for all four (YouTube does not report them).

prompt: In early 2026, rank these AI chatbots by the share of U.S. adults who say they use them.
explanation: ChatGPT (44%) is used by nearly twice as many U.S. adults as Gemini (24%). Meta AI is at 14% and Claude at 6%; Copilot (17%) and Grok (8%) fall in between. About half of adults (51%) use no AI chatbot at all.

source.title: Americans and AI 2026: Chatbots, Smart Devices and Views on Impact

extraSources.title: Americans report using ChatGPT far more than other chatbots (chart)

caveat: Self-reported 'ever use'; people may use Gemini or Meta AI inside other products without counting it.

prompt: In 2026, what percent of U.S. adults said the increased use of AI in daily life makes them feel more concerned than excited?
explanation: About half of U.S. adults (52%) are more concerned than excited, up from 50% in 2025 and 37% in 2021. Only 9% are more excited than concerned, and 37% feel equally concerned and excited.

source.title: Democrats are now more worried than Republicans about AI and its impact on jobs

extraSources.title: How Americans View AI and Its Impact on Human Abilities, Society

caveat: Survey of 3,488 U.S. adults on Pew's American Trends Panel; the 2025 reading (50%) is from June 9–15, 2025.

prompt: In 2026, what percent of U.S. adults said they are online "almost constantly"?
explanation: 44% of U.S. adults say they are online almost constantly, up from 41% in 2025. Another 41% go online several times a day; only about 5% go online less often than several times a week or not at all.

extraSources.title: Internet use, smartphone ownership and digital divides in the U.S.

prompt: In 2026, what share of U.S. adults said they regularly get news on TikTok?
explanation: One in five U.S. adults (20%) regularly get news on TikTok, the same as 2025 but up from 3% in 2020. Among adults under 30 it is 39%; among those 65 and older, 4%.

source.title: 1 in 5 Americans regularly get news on TikTok

prompt: In late 2025, what share of U.S. adults lived in a home that still had a landline phone?
explanation: About 20% of U.S. adults live in a household with a landline (18.6% landline plus wireless, 1.0% landline only). 80.0% live in wireless-only households, up from 76.0% two years earlier.

source.publisher: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
source.title: Wireless Substitution: Early Release of Estimates from the National Health Interview Survey, July–December 2025

caveat: Household-level measure for adults; the 2025 sample was reduced because the federal shutdown paused fieldwork in October–November 2025.

prompt: In 2026, what share of U.S. adults ages 18–29 said they use Facebook?
explanation: 69% of 18-to-29-year-olds say they use Facebook, about the same as adults overall (70%) and more than use TikTok (65%) or Snapchat (56%) in that age group. Only Instagram (79%) and YouTube (95%) reach more young adults.

source.title: Americans' Use of Social Media in 2026 (Social Media Fact Sheet)

caveat: 'Ever use' includes light or occasional use (e.g., Marketplace, groups); it says nothing about how often.
